speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) what lessons have the Ministry learnt from network disruptions experienced by a major telecommunications company in Singapore for three consecutive days; (b) whether the Ministry is aware of any disruptions of emergency or essential services contributed by the network disruptions; and (c) what steps are being considered by IMDA to prevent or minimise similar occurrences in the future.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information arising from the recent service disruptions affecting Singtel customers over three consecutive days, whether IMDA will review and strengthen its requirements on telecommunications network resilience, including ensuring that failover systems are robust and effective under real-world conditions.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information in view of the recent Singtel mobile service outage on 16 March 2026 which caused much business and personal disruption, whether the Ministry will consider introducing regulations to require telecommunications networks to facilitate temporary mobile service switches to subscribers affected by disruptions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) what are the causes of the 16 March 2026 disruption on Singtel’s mobile network; (b) how many users were affected; and (c) whether IMDA has any plan to review the minimum level of redundancy required for telecommunications networks, given increasing reliance for mobile services.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If Members are satisfied with the response, they may wish to withdraw their questions after this session.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A separate incident reported on 17 March affected about 2,000 Singtel mobile customers and was attributed to a software bug from a planned IT system update.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On 18 March, some Singtel mobile customers experienced intermittent connectivity issues during peak network traffic in the late afternoon.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singtel indicated that these issues were resolved within an hour.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) is investigating the incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thus far, there is no evidence that the incidents were due to cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA is also investigating whether calls to emergency services were affected by the incidents, even though there are no such reports thus far.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Service providers are held to high service standards through the Telecommunications Act and the Telecom Service Resiliency Code.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among other measures, service providers are required to conduct regular audits on key telecom infrastructure for resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are also required to uphold stringent quality of service standards, such as ensuring more than 99% nation-wide outdoor mobile service coverage at all times.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While disruptions cannot always be prevented, IMDA requires key service providers, like Singtel, to put in place robust measures to contain their impact and ensure speedy recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes providing redundancies and failover systems for core network functions.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA also regularly reviews its regulatory frameworks to ensure that they remain relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes updating regulations to protect our submarine cables in 2022 and to enhance the cybersecurity of key telecom operators in 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA is reviewing telecom service resilience regulations to ensure they remain effective.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It has been about three weeks since the incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We note that Singtel has provided one-time rebates for affected mobile subscribers as part of their service recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will publish its findings after investigations are completed and will not hesitate to take strong regulatory action should any lapses be identified.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These will be assessed for the ongoing review of telecom service resilience regulations, together with other suggestions that IMDA or the industry have put forward.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Teo, I assume that your response covers Parliamentary Question Nos 71 to 74 in today's Order Paper?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Can I just ask for clarification on the three incidents of Singtel disruption?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It was reported by the press that they were totally unrelated.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: What was the preliminary investigation based on the finding of IMDA?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And thirdly, will the service recovery be part of the requirement by IMDA or MDDI for other telecom companies (telcos) with similar incidents?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because investigations are still ongoing, I will not want to prejudge the outcome.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to the question that the Member raised about the compensation, this was done on Singtel's own volition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Around the world, if we look at various jurisdictions, we do not know of anyone that require telcos to make compensation for service disruptions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Part of the reason is because in most markets, telecom services are quite competitive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Meaning that from the provider standpoint, there is an interest on their part to maintain goodwill with their customers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, in this instance, Singtel has decided that the service disruption lasted long enough.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And they decided that they would offer a one-time rebate as part of their own service recovery.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, whether IMDA currently mandates stress testing or simulation of failover systems under peak or adverse conditions and if not, whether such requirements will be introduced following IMDA's review.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Second, even if such continuous incidents are infrequent, the impact of such disruptions on both consumers and businesses is significant, and I feel there should be greater safeguards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, will IMDA consider introducing more stringent resilience benchmarks on the telcos?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The stress testing obviously has to take place, but as we complete the investigations, we may find that there are parts of a system where the stress testing is not as good as it needs to be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, this will then inform our understanding of the extent to which we need to then strengthen the regulations and put in place the right set of obligations and expectations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I can assure the Member that we will take this very seriously.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Just to say that our telecom networks have become much more complex.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: From 3G to 4G to 5G and of course, in today's context, the system is also needing to respond to greater user needs, for example, in AI-enabled tools.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We fully appreciate what the Member has said.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members of the public, whether businesses or individuals, are depending on these services, so in terms of their reliability, the expectation is certainly rightly high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we look at telecom incidents and look at the period 2016 to 2020, compared to 2021 to 2025 – two big blocks, because annual numbers may not be fully reflective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And part of the purpose of investigations is to arrive at a better understanding of how the system components are interacting with one another and where we need to strengthen the measures.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: If IMDA in view of resiliency of our telephone network, would they consider regulations for them to work together, such that if there is any outage, there will be automatic switch-over from one telco to another telco, so that services to the subscribers are not disrupted?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: A simple example would be like we move to another country or we visit another country, and then we auto roam.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I am a telco engineer, so I know a little bit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But preliminarily, I would say that, even if there was mobile switching available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would not be able to respond to all kinds of service disruptions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It depends on which part of the network has gone down.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And maybe some parts of the network can be switchable between telcos, some parts of the network will not be able to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There maybe other kinds of mobile switching options available, but they will inevitably involve some cost, and it is not clear that subscribers are willing to pay for these additional features.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is something that we also have to keep in mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should add that in the Singapore context, wireless services are readily available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, looking at the issue from the point of view of a user, if you are able to get to a wireless network, there are also messaging services that you can rely on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the option that many people currently rely on and remains something that is quite viable.

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: I just wanted to ask the Minister, for outages, as we have spoken in this House, consumers and businesses are most affected.

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: One of the things that, if we hear from the ground, is that there is no real-time live information on how long the outages are going to be, what is the reasons for it and so on.

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: I understand, like in Australia, they have a live outage register.

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: Would the IMDA consider mandating telcos to provide real-time live information whenever any of these outages occur, rather than for consumers and businesses to wait for them to issue a press statement before finding out more information about these issues?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, quite a lot of the information on outages is crowdsourced.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is something called "Downdetector" that people very frequently refer to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By and large, it is quite reliable and it gives a very good sense of what is going on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In terms of our investigations, in terms of how we assess the incident response by the service providers, we will also look at how well they have done in terms of communicating with their subscribers and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The $5 to $10 goodwill rebates given out by Singtel and GOMO are not legally mandated, and these amounts may be small compared to the losses suffered by customers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that in some European countries, consumers actually do have a legal right to compensation in the event of service failures.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If the Ministry will not mandate compensation, what accessible recourse is available to consumers and small businesses to recover financial losses due to these network failures, given that legal action may be prohibitive?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that financial penalties for service lapses are high enough to act as a genuine deterrent, rather than a cheaper alternative to investing in network reliability, especially at the higher end of the reliability range?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And next, given the recent history of state-sponsored cyberattacks on our telcos, did IMDA and the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) conduct their own independent and thorough cybersecurity investigations beyond Singtel's internal investigations to arrive at their own conclusions and if so, did they uncover anything new?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some instances, with bigger customers, they may indeed have built into their contracts conditions upon which compensation would be due.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are not privy to all the details of these arrangements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I can say to the Member that they do exist.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some customers may already be seeking damages from the telco service providers when an incident of this nature happens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And when he talks about some European jurisdictions, we are only aware of the United Kingdom and Germany having in place arrangements that he may be referring to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think a competitive market does have this effect on the service providers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They know not to assume that the customers cannot change providers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is one feature of the way the market works that gives the consumers some assurance that the service providers need to be up to mark in terms of service resilience and reliability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The other thing is that in response to the earlier question by Mr Melvin Yong, I had cited how the regulations have also helped to reduce the number of incidents as well as the average duration per incident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And we will continue to look at how regulations can be strengthened in support of such improvements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have, on previous occasions, updated the public about findings that could be made known.
